title: Shifted local derived comparison with naturality with independent coefficient universe
statement: Let C be a category with Grothendieck topology J, R a sheaf of commutative rings, U an object, and choose a derived category of R|U-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Let I′ and I be K-injective complexes [def-pur-kinjective-complex], L′ and L arbitrary cochain complexes [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], s:I′→I and t:L′→L arbitrary chain maps, and n any integer. Degree-n homology of sections of Hom(L,I′) [def-pur-hom-complex] is equivalent to Hom_D(L|U,(I′|U)[n]), and similarly for Hom(L′,I). There exist these two equivalences for which the homology map induced by s and t is sent to derived precomposition by t|U and postcomposition by (s|U)[n]. Neither s nor t is assumed a quasi-isomorphism. This universe-general form takes C : Type u with Category v and coefficient/module universe max u v r, for arbitrary r; assume abelian-group sheafification and its locally bijective characterization on the original site. It uses the same sheaves, restriction, Hom complex, differentials, and induced maps as the original source statement.

source.place: Equation 21.34.0.1 (0A8Y), Lemma 21.34.6 (0A94), and naturality of componentwise composition

proof.text: Work with objects in Type u, arrows in Type v, and coefficient rings and modules in Type (max u v r). Use the existing siteAbelianHasSheafify and siteAbelianWEqualsLocallyBijective instances on the slice whenever an abelian or exactness instance is needed. All these instances are proved, and the given base-site instances are retained.

Obtain the two natural shifted section Hom-complex equivalences into the localized homotopy category. This is the section/cocycle/boundary part of the argument, with no K-injectivity or derived-category assumptions.

Restriction preserves K-injectivity; Mathlib supplies K-injectivity of shifts and Qh_map_bijective. Compose each homotopy equivalence with Qh.map and Iso.homCongr for quotientCompQhIso. The named zero-preservation theorem supplies restriction on complexes.

Rewrite the homotopy naturality equation, apply functoriality of Qh, and use quotientCompQhIso_hom_naturality and quotientCompQhIso_inv_naturality_assoc. Associativity gives the unchanged derived naturality equation.
